# Humus

> An opinionated Go framework for building services on bedrock's process model. Humus is being rebuilt, package by package, and these pages document what has landed. Releases up to v0.15.0, which pkg.go.dev shows by default, document the Builder/Runner, YAML configuration and rest.Run API that the rebuild removed.

## Docs

- [Humus](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/index.html.md): An opinionated Go framework for building services on bedrock's process model. Humus is being rebuilt, package by package, and these pages document what has landed. Releases up to v0.15.0, which pkg.go.dev shows by default, document the Builder/Runner, YAML configuration and rest.Run API that the rebuild removed.
- [The App lifecycle](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/lifecycle/index.html.md): How humus.Main builds a humus.App, and how the App reads its settings, builds its telemetry and its dependencies, runs its Services, drains and shuts them down within a grace period and turns the outcome into an exit status.
- [Serving HTTP](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/http/index.html.md): How to serve HTTP with the httpserver package: an Init that sources httpserver.Settings and returns the Service from NewService, the certificate it requires, the protocols it serves, how it drains and shuts down on httpserver.Main's defaults, what it records, and how to test it with httpservertest.
- [Calling HTTP services](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/http-client/index.html.md): How to call HTTP dependencies with the httpclient package: one client per dependency, built in Init from httpclient.Settings sourced with config.Struct, TLS and plain text, which requests are retried and how the end user's Classify decides what an answer means, Retry-After and the timeouts, the circuit breaker and its log records, the body rules, HTTP/2 behind a Kubernetes Service, what it records, and how to test the calls against a fake dependency.
- [Health](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/health/index.html.md): How a humus service reports its health: monitors and how they combine, what liveness and readiness each check, the health Service that owns an App's readiness through the lifecycle, and how httphealth and grpchealth expose the probes to Kubernetes, attached to a server the pod runs or on a probes port, with their answers, manifests, startup probes and tests.
- [Jobs](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/jobs/index.html.md): How to write a job with the job package: a run that job.NewService turns into a humus Service, the exit status Kubernetes sees for each way the run ends, which failures a Job retries, and how the run's span joins the trace of the process that started it.
- [Consuming and producing Kafka](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/kafka/index.html.md): How to consume and produce Kafka with the queue and queue/kafka packages: the contract a Processor keeps, an Init that sources kafka.Settings and returns the Service from NewService, what each Delivery commits and does with an error, how the consumer shuts down and rebalances on humus.Main's defaults, how a Producer built with NewProducer produces dead letters and events, what a call to Produce promises, its delivery timeout, circuit breaker and shutdown, what both record, and how to test them on kfake.
- [gRPC services](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/grpc/index.html.md): How to serve gRPC with the grpcserver package: an Init that sources grpcserver.Settings, registers generated services on the Service from NewService and returns it, the certificate it requires, what server options can change, how it ends streams and shuts down on grpcserver.Main's defaults, how Kubernetes' probes reach it, what it records, and how to test it with grpcservertest.
- [Calling gRPC services](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/grpc-client/index.html.md): How to call gRPC dependencies with the grpcclient package: one Client per dependency, built in Init from grpcclient.Settings sourced with config.Struct, TLS and plain text, names and addresses behind a ClusterIP or a headless Service and spreading load with the server's MaxConnectionAge, which calls are retried and how the end user's Classify decides what a code means, the pushback, the circuit breaker and its log records, streams, what it records, readiness with Connected, and how to test the end user's whole App next to a grpcserver backend.
- [Configuring a humus service](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/configuration/index.html.md): How a humus service's settings get their values: humus packages take plain Go values, and the service's Init sources each one, usually with bedrock's config package, so that a bad value fails startup with exit 78 and an error naming the variable.
- [Telemetry](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/telemetry/index.html.md): How a humus service gets its OpenTelemetry providers: the end user's Builder sources telemetry.Settings and calls telemetry.New, the App hands the SDK to Init, and humus never reads or sets OpenTelemetry's globals.
- [Testing a humus App](https://z5labs.github.io/humus/pr-preview/pr-845/testing/index.html.md): How to run a whole humus App inside a test with humustest.Start: the App humus.Main would run, under synctest, with no real socket, no file outside the test's temp directory and no secret in the repository.
